# dsh-subtitle-remover

A DSH Web UI plugin with a left-sidebar entry for
video-subtitle-remover:
pick a video, see a frame,

mark one or more subtitle regions on it (or let the
engine propose them), then run the job — or the

whole automatic path — without
leaving the Harness window.
## Install

1. Get video-subtitle-remover
working on the same machine: models downloaded, its `config/config.jso

n` in
place, and a Python environment with torch / paddle / cv2 installed.
2. Clone this repository

somewhere stable. Auto-detection covers these layouts — the
engine (`vsr`) and its environment (`vsr

-env`) either inside the plugin folder or
next to it / its `plugins/` parent:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[代码示例省略，未执行]

With any of these nothing needs configuring — the page's installer uses the
`engine/` layout by defa

ult. Any other layout works too — set `vsrRoot` /
`pythonPath` (see Configuration), or use the panel

to point at it.
3. Add it to DSH: on the Plugins page add this folder, or call the plugin
manager's

`install_bundle` with its absolute path.
4. Open the left sidebar entry `字幕擦除` / `Subtitle Remover`

`install_bundle` with its absolute path.
4. Open the left sidebar entry `字幕擦除` / `Subtitle Remover`.

## Screenshots

The editor: frame preview with the start/end processing range, drag-drawn regions, and
the detection

A finished job: the live before/after comparison strip kept from processing, per-job

## What it adds

- **Sidebar entry** `字幕擦除` / `Subtitle Remover` in the global panel list
(`sidebar.panellist`), with

a small pulse while a job runs.
- **A page** (`main` panel keyed by `subtitle-remover`) with:
- vid

eo path + directory picker (drives, folders, video files, sizes),
- `ffprobe` readout (resolution, f

ps, frame count, duration),
- **frame preview with a start/end time range** and a **region editor**:

drag to
draw a box, drag inside to move it, drag its bottom-right corner to resize; the
start frame

and end frame can both be inspected,
- **several regions at once** (up to 6), each also editable nu

merically,
- **automatic region detection** using the engine's own PP-OCR text detector on
sampled f

rames; the proposed boxes land in the same editor, so they stay
editable,
- **模型复核**: after detectio

n the plugin can hand the candidate bands and video
metadata to a DSH chat model (by default the one

selected in DSH, switchable
in the page), which decides which bands are real subtitles and which
in

painting model to use,
- **全自动处理 / Run automatically**: detect, let the model decide, then start the

job in one click,
- inpainting model + subtitle-detector choice, optional output folder,
- **处理区间**

: only frames between the start and end times are rewritten; the
rest of the video is copied through

untouched,
- **实时对比预览 / live comparison**: while the job runs, the engine's own preview
hook writes

a throttled before/after JPEG pair, so the page shows the original
and the cleaned frame side by si

de, frame number and percent included,
- live progress, frames, elapsed/remaining, speed, output pat

h + copy,
- **open-file / show-in-folder** on a finished job, in the job card and in each
history ro

w,
- **engine setup inside the page**: a scan of common locations, manual folder and
interpreter pic

kers (saved to the plugin, no profile editing), and a one-click
installer (clone + virtualenv + PyTo

rch/PaddlePaddle) for machines that don't
have the engine yet.
## How it talks to the engine

The Host half spawns the runners in `runner/` with the local checkout's
interpreter. Both print one

JSON event per line on a private channel
(`@@VSR@@ {...}`) while every engine/tqdm/paddle print goes

per line on a private channel
(`@@VSR@@ {...}`) while every engine/tqdm/paddle print goes to stderr:

- `vsr_runner.py` removes subtitles (one `--area` per marked region),
- `vsr_detect.py` samples fram

es, clusters the detected text boxes into bands and
reports them as percentages. Bands are ranked by

width, horizontal centring and
frame hits, so HUD text in a corner (ammo counters, kill feeds, mini

maps) loses
against the wide, centred subtitle line.

The page polls these over `/dsh-subtitle-remover/api/*` (registered on the
Harness webServer, same o
rigin, loopback + same-origin checked):
| Route | Purpose |

| `GET /state` | environment verdict, jobs, running detection |
| `GET /jobs`, `GET /jobs/<id>` | jo

b list / one job with its log |
| `POST /jobs`, `POST /jobs/<id>/cancel`, `POST /jobs/<id>/remove` |

job lifecycle |
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- A working video-subtitle-remover checkout (models downloaded, `config/config.json` present).
- Its

Python environment (the one with torch/paddle/cv2 installed).
- `ffmpeg` for the preview frame (the

checkout ships one, so this normally works
out of the box) and `ffprobe` for the metadata readout.
## Security

The HTTP surface is registered on the GUI's own origin and answers only loopback
requests whose `Hos

t` is loopback and whose `Origin`, when present, matches the
GUI. The image routes (`/frame`, `/jobs
//preview/*`) additionally refuse cross-site embeds through `Sec-Fetch-Site`, because an ``

on another local
page would otherwise be able to display arbitrary local pictures. The
`/jobs/<id>/

open` route only ever opens that job's own output path — it never
accepts a caller-supplied path. Th

ere is no authentication beyond the desktop
app's own renderer credential gate, so never expose the

GUI port to other
machines.
